To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the positive feedback loop of Rabex- 5/Rabaptins-5/Rab-5 in the endosomal membrane requires above endogenous Rab5 and Rabaptins-5 levels, which is a new phenomenon that we term delayed response.
the indirect pathway for Rab5 activation via Rabex-5 contains a threshold and the presence of the direct Rabex-5-mediated pathway reduces the delay in the onset of the activation.

(1) the indirect pathway constitutes the positive feedback loop for Rab5 activation; (2) the onset of this positive loop is delayed, which requires above normal levels of Rabex- 5 in the cell; (3) the presence of the direct pool of Rabex5 reduces the delay and facilitates the onset of positive feedback loop; and (4) our data quantitatively reveal the affinity of the Rabex5/Rabaptins/Rab5-GDP interaction in the cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of Rab5 activation and its regulation in the cell.
the relationship between the direct and indirect mechanisms in the activation of Rab5 in the cell, and the quantitative characterization of the positive feedback effect in Rab5 activation.
the quantitative understanding of the Rabex/Rabaptin/Rab5-mediated positive feedback pathway in the cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the positive feedback loop is not only important for the function of the endocytic machinery, but is also a sensitive mechanism that allows the cell to regulate the endocytic pathway in response to the levels of Rabex- 5, Rab5, and other components in the cell.

the direct pathway provides the basal activity and the indirect pathway provides the positive feedback loop, and the combination of both pathways provides the optimal activity for the early endosome fusion.

the direct pathway is the main pathway for Rabex-5 to activate Rab5 in the cell, and the positive feedback pathway mediated by Rabex-–5 and Rabapti–5 only contributes a small amount to the total Rab5 activation in early endosome fusion.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the direct pathway is required for the onset and the indirect pathway is required for maintenance of positive feedback activation of Rab5.
the direct and indirect pathway of Rab5 activation by Rabex- 5 are functionally interdependent and cooperate to promote Rab5-mediated endosome fusion and trafficking in the cell.
Rabex-5-mediated Rab5 activation on the endosome surface is a delayed positive feedback process, and the delay is shortened by the direct pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the indirect pathway of Rabex- 5 activation by the Rabex- 7/Rabaptin 5 complex is a positive feedback pathway that is delayed in onset.
the delayed response of the indirect pathway is a novel phenomenon that is not captured by the conventional mathematical models of Rabex- and Rabaptin-dependent Rab5 activation.
the positive feedback effect of Rabex- 5/Rabapti-5/Rab-5 on early endosome fusion is delayed, which is a unique feature that is not shared by other positive feedback loops.
